column1: # fields_m2a.tsv — mapped gameplay fields compared at sync anchors
# Columns: name <TAB> base <TAB> addr <TAB> width <TAB> phase <TAB> note
#   base:  abs (addr = absolute RAM address) | p1 ($FF8400 + addr) | p2 ($FF8800 + addr)
#   phase: stable  = compare at every follow offset (identity/stat fields)
#          settled = compare only at offsets >= --settle (default 120): valid
#                    once the round has settled into neutral idle — during the
#                    intro these are mid-animation and legitimately differ
#                    cross-emulator by a few frames of phase slip
#          phase   = anim-cursor-derived; compared only in --exact mode
# Reviewable data, not code (CLAUDE.md rule 5). The anchor predicate itself
# 14z-90 (GitHub issue #16): p1/p2_char_id at +0x382 REMOVED from the
# dual-emulator field set. 14z-87 measured that byte as the voice-flavor
# class in match, reassigned by the engine from the opponent's candidate
# row — and measured the borrow as a cross-emulator LOTTERY (0x06/0x0C/
# 0x09/0x00 on MAME vs 0x04 on FBNeo, identical inputs). It is the one
# field here known to disagree between the two codebases BY DESIGN, so
# comparing it at every anchor asserts a disagreement. In-match identity
# is carried by p1/p2_hitbox_base at +0x60 below.
# METER (14z-94, GitHub #83). CLAUDE.md §4 names meter in the dual-emulator
# protocol's mapped set — "character IDs, HP, positions, timer, meter, and the
# other fields in ram.md" — and this map omitted both halves of it, so a
# cross-emulator meter regression passed the stage-4 oracle while every
# mapped field agreed. ram.md:113-114. The existing dump windows already
# cover $FF8509/$FF8909, so nothing else had to change.
